newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&Ps ease slightly after Tuesday's rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&Ps ease slightly after Tuesday's rally.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor's 500 futures were slightly lower on profit-taking from Tuesday's rally which was one of the market's largest single-day advances, traders and analysts said.
Open interest in June S&Ps increased 4,626 to 182,378 on Tuesday, suggestive of new buying. T-bond futures' preliminary open interest rose more than 16,000 to about 513,300.

Some traders speculated that the short-covering rally in S&Ps, which was born amid light volume and from modest advances in U.S. bonds, extended so high as to draw buying from pension and fund managers and asset allocators.
"Managers may have perceived the rally as substantial and just decided to put money to work," one S&P futures trader said.
Some S&P futures analysts also said the post-April 15 income tax deadline may have contributed to the fresh flow of money into the market.

June S&Ps weakened slightly on GLOBEX and widened opening losses to 778.40 even though cash S&Ps were initially higher. Traders said futures were adjusting to fair value after June closed slightly above fair value on Tuesday.
Current fair value stands at 4.30 points, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 5.30 points and arbitrage sell programs are about 3.30 points over.

Traders and analysts said Wednesday's retreat was corrective and did not rule out a possible rally later in the day. One floor trader said June S&Ps could test 782.50, the 50-percent retracement from the contract's all-time high of 827.80 to last Monday's 4-1/2-month low of 736.40.
"It's healthy," Donald Selkin, head of stock index futures trading at Prudential Securities Inc, said about the light selloff this morning.
Selkin noted technology stocks, which have been lagging, were rebounding early Wednesday, while the larger-cap stocks that rallied on Tuesday were slightly softer.
"The rally is broadening out a little, and it's healthy because at least the troops are trying to keep up the generals," he said.

At 0948 CDT/1448 GMT, June S&Ps were down 1.75 at 779.05, KCBT Value Lines were down 1.00 at 687.70, new composites were off 1.65 at 407.55, Nikkeis were up 90 at 18,780, Midcap 400s were 0.30 lower at 252.40, Nasdaq 100s were 10.00 higher at 836.50 and Russell 2000s were 0.20 higher at 340.50.
